title: Choosing something to eat
examples: I cannot decide what to eat tonight.
Let's make the choice smaller. Would something warm or something cold feel easier tonight?
Nothing in the fridge appeals to me.
Start with the easiest ingredient you have. It only needs to become a manageable meal, not an exciting one.
I have looked at delivery menus for an hour.
Choose one familiar place, then one meal you usually enjoy. You can stop comparing once that choice is made.
What is a low effort dinner?
Toast with eggs, beans, or another topping you enjoy can be a starting point. Add something fresh if it is available.
I want dinner without lots of washing up.
A filled wrap or a simple sandwich can keep the dishes down. Choose a filling that suits your needs.
I need someone to narrow my food options.
Let's choose between two: a simple pasta meal or a filled sandwich. Which sounds more manageable?
I keep changing my mind about lunch.
Pick something familiar that fits what you have. Lunch does not have to be the best possible choice.
Everyone at home wants a different meal.
Could you share one base, like rice or bread, and let people choose their own toppings?
I am too tired to follow a recipe.
An assembled meal counts. Put together a few ready to eat foods you like, without turning it into a cooking project.
Can you choose a meal from what I own?
Tell me a few ingredients you have and any dietary needs. We can then narrow the options together.
live

title: Food when time is short
examples: I have ten minutes before my next meeting.
Use that time for something straightforward to eat. A sandwich or leftovers may be enough to get lunch started.
I need breakfast I can take with me.
Try preparing something portable that you enjoy, such as overnight oats or a filled roll, when you have a moment.
I cannot cook today.
You can still have a meal. Ready to eat ingredients and prepared food are useful options on a day like this.
I need a meal with almost no chopping.
Frozen vegetables, tinned pulses, and ready prepared ingredients can reduce the preparation. Choose what works for your kitchen.
I have only one clean bowl.
A bowl of cereal, soup, or a simple rice meal could work. Start with food; the rest can wait.
Can frozen food count as a proper meal?
Yes. Frozen ingredients and prepared meals can be useful parts of everyday eating. Follow the preparation instructions.
I need something after getting home late.
Keep the decision gentle. A familiar, easy meal is enough tonight; it does not need extra steps.
I forgot to defrost anything.
Look for food you can use safely as it is, or cook from frozen if the label allows it. You can change the plan.
My lunch break got cut short.
See whether you can protect a few minutes to eat now, and make room for more food later if you need it.
I need a backup meal for busy nights.
Choose one shelf or freezer meal you already like. Keep its ingredients together so there is less to think about.

title: Use what is already here
examples: I have pasta and a tin of tomatoes.
That can be a simple starting point. If you have beans, lentils, or another protein you enjoy, you could add some.
I have rice but no dinner plan.
Think of rice as the base. Check for a suitable topping, some vegetables, and a sauce or seasoning you enjoy.
How do I use up these vegetables?
Tell me which vegetables you have and whether they are still fresh. We can find a simple way to use them.
live
I keep buying ingredients I already own.
Before your next shop, take a quick look at one cupboard and the fridge. A short list can be enough.
My cupboards are full but I feel like there is no food.
Pick one familiar meal, then check only for its ingredients. You do not need to organise every cupboard first.
I want to clear a little freezer space.
Choose one item you can safely use this week. Build a meal around that before adding anything new.
Can you suggest a meal from a photo of my fridge?
A photo may miss labels, dates, and ingredients. Tell me what is there and any food restrictions before we choose.
live
I bought too many fresh ingredients.
Choose one to use soon. Check reliable storage or freezing guidance for the others, so you do not have to rush through everything.
I cannot remember when I opened this food.
Check its label and reliable food safety guidance. If you cannot establish that it is safe, choose something else.
live
Can you tell if this leftover is safe to eat?
I cannot confirm food safety from a description alone. Storage time, temperature, and the food itself all matter.
live

title: An easier food shop
examples: Put milk on my food list.
Open your food shopping list to add milk. This recording cannot save the item for you.
tool
Add the ingredients for tomorrow's dinner.
First choose the meal and check what you already have. The remaining ingredients can go on your food shopping list.
tool
What should I buy for three easy meals?
Start with three meals you know you will eat. Reusing a few ingredients can make the list shorter.
I get overwhelmed at the supermarket.
A short list grouped by section may help. You can shop for a few days instead of solving the whole week.
I keep forgetting a key ingredient.
Write the meal name beside its ingredients. Before leaving, check the list against what you already have.
Can you read my shopping list aloud?
Your saved list needs to be opened before its items can be read. A prepared recording cannot know what is on it.
tool
Remove bread from my shopping list.
You can remove bread in the food shopping list. Check the right item before deleting it.
tool
I need a small shop, not a huge weekly shop.
Choose food for your next few meals and one easy backup. A shorter list is a valid plan.
I buy too much when I go shopping.
Try starting with meals you realistically expect to make. Leave room for convenience, rather than planning an ambitious week.
Can you order all my groceries?
Daywell does not place grocery orders. You can use your food list as a reference when ordering from your chosen shop.
live

title: A flexible meal plan
examples: Meal planning feels like too much work.
Plan just one meal ahead. You can repeat something familiar and leave the rest of the week open.
I never stick to a weekly menu.
Try a small set of options rather than fixed meals for every day. You can choose based on your energy.
Can I eat the same lunch a few days in a row?
Repeating a lunch you enjoy can simplify things. Aim for variety across your eating over time, without making each meal complicated.
I need a meal plan that leaves room for changes.
Include a quick backup meal and keep some ingredients flexible. A plan can support your day without controlling it.
I am feeding people with different tastes.
Meals with separate toppings or sides can offer choice without several completely different dinners.
I want to prepare food ahead without spending Sunday cooking.
Choose one useful preparation step, such as washing produce or making a portion for later. You can stop there.
I planned five dinners but only cooked one.
That tells you the plan asked for too much this week. Try fewer cooking nights and more easy options next time.
Can you make my entire meal plan personal to me?
I would need your preferences, budget, schedule, and dietary needs. Medical nutrition plans should involve a qualified professional.
live
I want a simple way to plan tomorrow's food.
Think about when you will be home and when you will be out. Choose one realistic food option for each part of the day.
My family meal plan changes every evening.
Keep a few adaptable ingredients available if you can. The plan can be a set of possibilities rather than a promise.

title: A manageable breakfast
examples: Breakfast feels like another task.
Make it as familiar as possible. Keep an easy option where you can find it without searching.
I leave home before I feel ready to eat.
Could you take something with you for later? Make space for food in a way that fits your morning.
I need a breakfast without cooking.
Cereal, yoghurt with fruit, or a sandwich could be options, depending on what you enjoy and can eat.
I want a warm breakfast with little effort.
Porridge or toast with a familiar topping can be a simple option. Follow the preparation instructions for what you use.
I forget breakfast when mornings are busy.
Put a gentle reminder beside something you already do in the morning. Keep the food choice easy.
I cannot face a large breakfast.
You do not have to force a large meal. Start with something manageable, and seek advice if low appetite keeps making eating difficult.
Can breakfast just be leftovers?
Breakfast does not need special breakfast food. Safely stored and reheated leftovers can be an option you enjoy.
I need breakfast ideas for a hotel room.
Look for simple food you can store safely, or check what the hotel offers. You can keep the choice familiar.
I have got bored of my usual breakfast.
Change one part, such as the fruit or topping, before replacing the whole routine.
I want to prepare tomorrow's breakfast tonight.
Choose an option that stores safely overnight. Set out what you need so the morning has fewer steps.

title: Make room for lunch
examples: I work through lunch almost every day.
Could you protect a short break to eat today? Your work can have a pause without needing to be finished first.
I have no lunch packed.
Look for one accessible option nearby or at home. You can solve today's lunch without fixing the whole routine.
I want a lunch that travels well.
Choose food you can keep at a safe temperature. A suitable container and storage plan matter as much as the recipe.
I eat lunch while answering emails.
If it is possible, close the messages for the first few bites. Give yourself one small part of the break back.
The staff room makes lunch stressful.
Is there another suitable place where you could eat more comfortably? You can choose a quieter break when circumstances allow.
I keep reaching afternoon without eating.
A visible lunch reminder may help interrupt the rush. Keep a practical food option ready for when the reminder appears.
I need lunch that does not need a microwave.
A sandwich, filled wrap, or suitable cold meal could work. Make sure you can store it safely until lunchtime.
Can you remind me to take lunch tomorrow?
Use a reminder you can verify in your calendar or alarm tool. This recording does not create a notification.
tool
I only have leftovers for lunch.
Leftovers can make lunch easier. Check how they were stored and follow safe reheating guidance where needed.
I feel guilty stopping work to eat.
Eating is an ordinary need. A lunch break does not have to be earned by getting through the whole list.

title: Dinner after a full day
examples: I get home and cannot start dinner.
Sit down for a moment if you need to. Then choose the easiest available meal, with as few steps as possible.
Cooking after work drains me.
You can use prepared ingredients, repeat meals, or choose something ready made. Dinner does not need to become a second shift.
I ordered takeaway again and feel bad.
One food choice does not define how you look after yourself. Notice what made cooking difficult and plan a useful backup.
I want dinner to feel comforting.
Think of a familiar meal you enjoy. Comfort can come from something simple, warm, and easy to settle with.
I am eating alone tonight.
You can make the meal pleasant for yourself too. Choose somewhere comfortable and food that fits the evening you have.
I have ingredients but the kitchen is a mess.
Clear just enough space to prepare something safely. The whole kitchen does not need to be finished before you eat.
Can you make dinner happen in three steps?
Choose the meal, gather only its ingredients, then follow its cooking instructions. Keep tonight's choice simple.
Dinner is going wrong and I am getting upset.
Pause and make the kitchen safe first. You can switch to an easier meal; the original plan does not need rescuing at any cost.
I do not want to cook a special meal just for myself.
A small, familiar meal is enough. You are allowed convenience even when you are the only person eating.
I want tomorrow's dinner to be easier.
Choose the meal before tomorrow gets busy. Check its ingredients and any safe preparation you can do ahead.

title: Something between meals
examples: I need an easy snack idea.
Try something you enjoy and can eat comfortably, such as fruit, toast, or yoghurt. Check it suits your dietary needs.
Is it okay to have a snack?
Snacks can be part of everyday eating. You do not need to turn having something to eat into a moral decision.
I need a snack for a long journey.
Choose food that travels and stores safely. Keep it easy to reach when you are stopped somewhere safe to eat.
I want a snack but cannot decide which one.
Would you prefer something crunchy or something soft? One small choice can narrow it down.
I get hungry while making dinner.
You can have something to eat while dinner is being prepared. You do not have to wait until you are uncomfortable.
I forgot to take food on my trip.
At your next safe opportunity, look for an accessible food option. Taking care of that need is part of the journey.
I need snacks I can keep at my desk.
Look for food with suitable storage instructions and packaging. Keep a couple of options you actually like.
I always judge myself for evening snacks.
Try describing what happened without blame. If food worries keep taking over, support from a qualified professional may help.
Can I include sweet food in my week?
Enjoyment can be part of eating. You can think about the overall pattern without labelling a single food choice as a failure.
I want to stop using exercise to earn snacks.
Food does not need to be earned through movement. If that rule feels hard to let go of, consider talking with an eating disorder professional.
live

title: Food alongside strength training
examples: What foods contain protein?
Beans, lentils, tofu, eggs, dairy, fish, and meat are examples. Choose options that fit your preferences and dietary needs.
Can I get protein from plant foods?
Beans, lentils, tofu, and other plant foods can contribute protein. A varied eating pattern can help you include different nutrients.
Do I have to buy protein powder?
Protein powder is not essential for everyone. Ordinary food can provide protein, and personal needs are worth discussing with a qualified dietitian.
I want to eat well while getting stronger.
Regular meals, enough food overall, and suitable protein sources can support training. A personalised plan depends on your needs.
How much protein should I eat for my body?
That depends on factors including your health and activity. A registered dietitian can help work out an appropriate amount.
live
I need a simple protein option for lunch.
You could add beans, tofu, egg, fish, or another suitable food you enjoy to a familiar lunch.
Can you tell me which supplement to buy?
I cannot choose supplements safely without your health context. A pharmacist or qualified clinician can help check suitability and interactions.
live
I think I have to eat perfectly to build strength.
A workable eating routine matters more than making every plate feel perfect. Leave room for ordinary meals and enjoyment.
I cannot afford expensive gym food.
You do not need food marketed for the gym. Everyday ingredients can be useful, including beans, lentils, and other affordable options.
Can you give me a muscle gain diet?
A suitable plan needs more information about your health, preferences, and training. A qualified dietitian can help personalise it.
live

title: Finding an eating rhythm
examples: I forget to eat when I am absorbed in something.
Try placing an eating break beside a regular part of your day. A visible reminder can help you notice the time.
My eating routine disappears on busy days.
Keep one reliable, easy food option available. The backup can support you when the usual routine does not fit.
I want fewer all or nothing food rules.
Choose one supportive habit rather than a strict list of restrictions. Make it something you can adapt when life changes.
I cannot tell whether I am hungry anymore.
That can be difficult to navigate alone. A qualified clinician or dietitian can help you find a safe eating routine.
live
I missed a meal and now feel behind.
You do not have to make the day perfect again. Think about your next practical opportunity to eat something.
How can I remember to take food to work?
Put a note beside your keys or bag, and prepare what you can safely in advance. Keep the reminder visible.
My schedule changes every day.
Try planning around events, like leaving home or finishing a shift, instead of relying only on fixed meal times.
I want a gentle food reminder without calorie talk.
You can use a simple reminder such as, have I made room to eat? No calorie target is needed for that prompt.
I have hardly eaten for several days.
Please speak to a healthcare professional promptly, especially if you feel weak or unwell. This needs more support than a food reminder.
live
Can you help me build a realistic food routine?
Start by identifying the part of the day when eating is hardest. We can make one small change around that moment.

title: A kinder relationship with food
examples: I feel like I ruined everything with one meal.
One meal is not a verdict on you. You can continue your day without punishing yourself or trying to undo it.
I want to skip dinner because I ate dessert.
Dessert does not mean you have lost permission to eat dinner. If these rules feel persistent, reach out for qualified support.
live
Can you shame me into eating better?
I will not use shame around food. We can look for a small, practical change that respects your needs.
I keep comparing my plate to everyone else's.
Other people's plates do not show their needs or their whole day. Bring the focus back to what supports your own eating.
Food tracking makes me anxious.
You can step away from tracking. If anxiety around food is growing, a qualified professional can help you find a gentler approach.
I do not want a weight loss goal.
You can focus on regular meals, enjoyment, and having energy for your day. A weight goal is not required.
I want you to call my food good or bad.
I would rather help you describe what a meal offers and what you enjoy. Moral labels can make eating feel harder.
I think I need to work off what I ate.
Movement does not need to repay food. If that pressure keeps coming back, consider support from an eating disorder professional.
live
I am frightened of eating more foods.
That sounds difficult. A qualified professional can help you work with that fear at a pace that is safe for you.
live
Can this app treat my eating disorder?
Daywell cannot treat an eating disorder. Please seek professional care; gentle app tools can only sit alongside appropriate support.
live

title: Food within your budget
examples: Healthy food feels too expensive.
Start with affordable foods you already use. Tinned and frozen options can help you build meals without needing speciality products.
I need to spend less on lunches.
Choose one lunch you could bring from home this week. Repeating an easy option can reduce both cost and decisions.
Can you plan food around a small budget?
Tell me your budget, what food you already have, and where you shop. Prices vary, so we would need to check the actual costs.
live
I keep wasting expensive ingredients.
Buy for fewer planned meals at a time if you can. Choose ingredients that work in more than one familiar dish.
Do I need organic ingredients to eat well?
You do not need to make organic food a requirement. Work with food that is accessible, affordable, and suitable for you.
I want a cheap meal with beans.
Beans can go into a jacket potato, a wrap, or a simple tomato sauce. Use the preparation directions on the label.
Cooking from scratch is not always cheaper for me.
Your time, equipment, and energy matter too. Choose the combination of prepared and homemade food that works in your circumstances.
I cannot buy every ingredient in this recipe.
Choose a simpler recipe or check which substitutions are suitable. A shorter ingredient list may fit your budget better.
I do not have enough money for food this week.
You deserve help with that. A local council, food support organisation, or trusted community service may be able to connect you with food.
live
Can you compare prices at my local shops?
Current prices need a live check. A saved recording cannot compare today's offers, but your shopping list can help organise the comparison.
live

title: Keep a useful food note
examples: Log the sandwich I just ate.
Open the food log and add the sandwich there. Check the saved entry so your record reflects what you intended.
tool
Show me what I ate yesterday.
Your food history needs to be opened to answer that. A prerecorded reply cannot see yesterday's entries.
tool
Can you calculate calories from this photo exactly?
A photo cannot provide an exact calorie count. Portions, ingredients, and preparation can be unclear, so estimates should be treated as uncertain.
live
I forgot to log a meal.
You can add a note later if it is useful. Your record does not need to be complete to offer something helpful.
I only want to record whether I ate regularly.
A simple note about meals can be enough. You do not need to record every ingredient or calorie for that purpose.
Delete an incorrect food entry.
Find the entry in your food history and check its details before removing it. This audio does not delete saved data.
tool
I want to remember a meal I enjoyed.
Write its name and the part you liked. That can become a useful option when choosing a future meal.
Is my food history private?
Check Daywell's current privacy information and settings before adding sensitive details. Only share what you are comfortable recording.
live
Can you see whether my eating has improved?
That would need your actual records and a clear idea of what improvement means to you. A saved reply cannot assess the pattern.
tool
I do not want meal logging to become a chore.
Keep only the details that help you. You can pause logging when it stops feeling useful.

title: Dietary needs and limits
examples: I have a food allergy; can you choose something safe?
Please check ingredient labels, allergen information, and your care advice. I cannot guarantee that a suggested meal is safe for your allergy.
live
Can I eat this if I have diabetes?
Your own care plan and medication matter. A qualified clinician or dietitian can advise on food choices for your diabetes.
live
I need food advice during pregnancy.
Please use pregnancy specific guidance from a qualified clinician or trusted health service. General meal ideas cannot check every safety consideration.
live
I am vegan; can you keep that in mind?
Vegan meal ideas are possible. Share any other dietary needs too, so the suggestions can fit your preferences.
live
My throat is swelling after eating something.
Call emergency services now. In the UK, call nine nine nine. If you have a prescribed adrenaline auto injector, use it according to your emergency plan.
urgent
Can you put my child on a diet?
Children's nutrition and growth need qualified guidance. Please speak with an appropriate healthcare professional instead of using an adult diet plan.
live
Can food cure my medical condition?
I cannot promise a cure through food. Speak with your healthcare team about nutrition that can support your treatment.
live
I need a diet for kidney disease.
Kidney conditions can require specific nutritional advice. Please work with your kidney care team or a specialist dietitian.
live
The recipe says may contain my allergen; is a little okay?
Do not rely on me to judge an allergy risk. Follow your allergy care advice and check with an appropriate professional.
live
I have been vomiting and cannot keep fluids down.
Please seek urgent medical advice, especially if you feel very unwell or dehydrated. In the UK, NHS one one one can guide you.
live
